title: throughput-degradation-investigation-labbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a running labbook for an active throughput degradation observed in the serving runtime across releases 2025.12 -> 2026.01. Goal: produce reproducible diagnostics, isolate root cause, and capture the bisect/canary comparison artifacts so we can automate detection and rollback policies.

High-level summary (short):
- Symptom: sustained 15-30% drop in tokens/sec on P100-like instances for batch workloads during mid-peak hours starting 2026-01-21 03:40 UTC.
- Impact: higher tail latency (p95 +100ms), queueing increases, autoscaler thrash on Dedicated pools.
- Initial hypothesis: a change in KV-cache eviction/serialization or a kernel selection fallback that increases per-token CPU work.

Measurement methodology (what we measure and where):
- Metrics sources: Prometheus (serving_metrics), Datadog traces (via ingest), local flamegraphs from perf and async-profiler, GPU utilization from nvidia-smi exporter, kernel-level counters via perf_event.
- Key metrics: generation_tokens/sec (per model, per instance); request_queue_length; model_cpu_us_per_token; kv_cache_hit_ratio; kernel_fallback_count; batch_size_distribution; p50/p95 token latency.
- Baseline window: 2025-12-10 -> 2026-01-19 (pre-regression). Incident window: 2026-01-21 -> present.

Quick triage checklist (for on-call):
1) Confirm alert triggers: which alert fired and threshold. Check alert rule: serving.runtime.throughput.drop > 20% over 30m.
2) Check related signals: p95 latency, queue length, rate-limiting events.
3) Identify affected model families (gpt-small, rw-meduim-xq, quantized variants).
4) Snapshot canary vs prod panels: tokens/sec by build tag + git commit sha.
5) If canary shows same degradation, escalate to perf triage. If only prod, focus on routing/traffic/scale.

PromQL snippets used during investigation:
- Tokens/sec per instance (30m avg): sum(rate(serving_tokens_generated_total[5m])) by (instance)
- KV cache hit ratio: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))
- Batch size distribution (approx): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le)(rate(serving_batch_size_bucket[5m])) )
- Kernel fallback counter: increase(kernel_fallback_total[30m]) > 0
Notes: tune time windows when comparing canary vs baseline to avoid diurnal noise.

Bisect protocol (engineering playbook):
Objective: find the earliest commit/deploy change correlated with throughput drop. Use both git bisect on serving runtime repo and deploy-tag bisect in infra.
Steps:
- Step A: reproduce with pinned build hashes. Pull images for the oldest-good (tag: 2025.12.7) and newest-bad (tag: 2026.01.20). Run local perf harness against a small node pool with traffic replay. If reproducible, proceed with git bisect.
- Step B: git bisect in serving-runtime repo:
  * git checkout main; git bisect start bad_sha good_sha
  * For each candidate commit, build image (make docker-build), push to test registry, deploy to isolated test cluster (k8s namespace perf-bisect-###), run 30m replay and collect the tokens/sec and kv-cache metrics.
  * Mark good/bad based on tokens/sec drop > 10% vs baseline.
- Step C: infra/ops bisect (if repo bisect fails): try rolling back infra components in this order: kernel modules, CUDA driver, system glibc, container runtime (containerd/docker), deployment config (envs), k8s CNI. Use canary-sized subsets.
Automation notes: we have a bisect helper script at tools/bisect/run_bisect.sh (see linked PR) that automates build/deploy/collect. Use --min-replication 3 to reduce false positives.

Canary comparison approach (how we compare two builds):
- Deploy candidate image and baseline side-by-side in the same region using traffic-split router (split by header X-Test-Bucket).
- Traffic pattern: replay production traces (last-week sample) with a bounded token budget so we don't overspend. Use 60% baseline / 40% candidate for 1 hour, then flip 40/60 for 1 hour.
- Panels to inspect: tokens/sec, request queue length, kv_cache_hit_ratio, p95 token latency, kernel_fallback_count, cpu utilization, host load avg.
- Use relative-delta panels: (candidate - baseline)/baseline * 100. Flag any metric delta > 10% as a hard signal.

Detailed hypothesis log (chronological):
- 2026-01-21 04:05 UTC: ops noticed autoscaler thrash in dedicated-pool-eu. Initial slack message: "tokens/sec drop across batch workloads; queues piling."
- 2026-01-21 06:30 UTC: Evelyn confirmed p95 up ~120ms, tokens/sec down 22% across quantized-llm-8bit models.
- 2026-01-21 10:12 UTC: quick canary (old image vs newest) run. Candidate showed 18% lower throughput; kv_cache_hit_ratio unchanged.
- 2026-01-22 12:00 UTC: Marcus ran profiler (async-profiler) during load: observed increased allocations in serialization path and higher Java/C++ transitions on request routing thread pool.
- 2026-01-23 09:00 UTC: Priya ran kernel counters: increase in branch-mispredicts and context-switches per token for bad build.
- 2026-01-25 15:30 UTC: started git bisect; narrowed to a merge that updated the dynamic-kv-serializer and a small change in kernel selection logic.

Collected artifacts and where to find them:
- Canary dashboards: Grafana link (internal) - see linked_artifacts page.
- Trace collection: datadog trace ids: trace:prod:2026-01-21:abc123, trace:test:2026-01-22:def456.
- Flamegraphs: s3://redwood-inference-perf/flamegraphs/2026-01-bisect/commit-9f2a7.svg
- Profiler snapshots: gs://perf-snapshots/serving-runtime/2026-01-22/async-profiler.tgz
- Bisect logs: tools/bisect/results/2026-01-bisect.log (attached to INF-3421)

Root-cause candidate and short-term mitigations:
- Candidate: a subtle change in dynamic-kv-serializer that increased copy-on-write behavior when prefix caching is disabled (seen on quantized path). This change interacts badly with the new kernel-selection fallback which forces a synchronous deserialization on the request thread. Net effect: more CPU per token and higher scheduler preemption.
- Short-term mitigations recommended:
  1) Revert dynamic-kv-serializer change in a patch release and monitor tokens/sec.
  2) As a lower-risk path, enable aggressive kv_cache_prefix_caching for affected pools (config flag) to reduce lookups.
  3) Put a temporary SLO-based rollback (automated) if tokens/sec delta > 15% for 30m on Dedicated.

Long-term fixes to consider:
- Add unit-level benchmarks that exercise the serialization path under synthetic batch shapes; run in PR gating (benchmark-ci).
- Improve async deserialization path so kernel fallback doesn't block request thread. Add microbenchmarks for kernel selection heuristics.
- Increase observability: expose per-request deserialization latency and a histogram of kernel selection path.

Investigation commands and snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- k8s: kubectl -n perf-bisect logs -l app=serving-runtime -c serving --since=1h | grep tokens/sec
- build: make docker-build && docker tag serving-runtime:local registry.test/redwood/serving-runtime:${SHA} && docker push ...
- perf capture (host): sudo perf record -g -F 99 -p <pid> -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 60; sudo perf script -i /tmp/perf.data | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.fold; flamegraph.pl out.fold > flame.svg
- async-profiler: ./profiler.sh -d 60 -e cpu -f /tmp/async.svg <pid>

False-positive checklist (what can mimic this incident):
- Noisy neighbor on same host (check node-level pod top CPU consumers).
- Misconfigured autoscaler or sudden traffic pattern change.
- Tooling/metric changes: ensure metric label renames didn't change; verify scraping targets.
- Version skew in dependencies (libtorch/cuda mismatch).

Open action items (owner/resolution):
- Jordan: run a full bisect iteration with --min-replication 5 and attach the raw test traces. DUE 2026-02-01. (work in progress)
- Evelyn: verify canary split replay scripts include token shape variation; add another workload mix. DUE 2026-01-28. (done)
- Marcus: instrument per-request deserialization timing and add histogram metric. DUE 2026-02-05. (in progress)
- Priya: coordinate short-term rollback with infra and legal for dedicated-pool impacts. DUE 2026-02-03. (in progress)

Notes to future readers:
- This doc is intentionally a labbook: expect partial commands, rough outputs, and links to live dashboards. When the incident is closed, we will move a cleaned-up writeup to Confluence with final RCA and the postmortem timeline.
- If you pick this up mid-stream, start by looking at the bisect logs and the 2026-01-25 profiler snapshots. They contain the most deterministic signals.

Appendix: quick decision rubric for rollback vs config flip:
- If tokens/sec drop > 15% AND p95 latency up > 75ms for 30m on >50% of Dedicated nodes -> automatic rollback.
- If tokens/sec drop 10-15% but kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.8 -> enable prefix caching and monitor for 2h.
- If kernel_fallback_count > 0 and correlates with higher branch-mispredicts -> prioritize kernel selection fix.

End of labbook entry. Keep adding timestamped notes in this same content field (append-only preferred).
